task.instructions:
Using matplotlib, build a 2x2 grid of subplots -- one panel per city -- showing each city's mean temperature across the four seasons.
Fill the grid in row-major order: top-left Oslo, top-right Cairo, bottom-left Sydney, bottom-right Nairobi.
In every panel plot the four seasons in the order Winter, Spring, Summer, Autumn along the x axis, as a line.
Mean temperature in degrees Celsius, in that season order:
Oslo: -3.5, 5.2, 17.1, 6.8
Cairo: 14.0, 22.5, 31.2, 24.1
Sydney: 18.3, 15.0, 9.1, 14.4
Nairobi: 19.2, 20.1, 18.0, 19.5
Every panel must have its own title naming that panel's city.
Every panel must also label both of its axes: the x label must contain "season" and the y label must contain "temperature".
Finally, give the whole figure an overall title (a suptitle) that contains the word "temperature".

cat <<'EOF' > create_climate_panels.py
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Data for each city
cities = {
    "Oslo": [-3.5, 5.2, 17.1, 6.8],
    "Cairo": [14.0, 22.5, 31.2, 24.1],
    "Sydney": [18.3, 15.0, 9.1, 14.4],
    "Nairobi": [19.2, 20.1, 18.0, 19.5]
}

# Seasons for x-axis labels
seasons = ["Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Autumn"]

# Create a 2x2 grid of subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 8))
fig.suptitle("Seasonal Temperature Comparison Across Cities")

# Fill the grid in row-major order
city_order = ["Oslo", "Cairo", "Sydney", "Nairobi"]
for i, city in enumerate(city_order):
    row = i // 2
    col = i % 2
    ax = axes[row, col]
    
    # Plot the data
    ax.plot(seasons, cities[city], marker='o')
    
    # Set title and labels
    ax.set_title(city)
    ax.set_xlabel("Season")
    ax.set_ylabel("Temperature (°C)")

# Adjust layout to prevent overlap
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig("figure.png")
plt.close()
EOF
